title: Output when the decision tape is blank
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean symbols, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, let $bits$ be a Boolean selector encoding, let $P$ be a valid input-head position for $y$, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$. Given auxiliary tape contents $\tau_C,\tau_O$, positions $z_C,z_O$, an optional state $oq$, an output register $r$, and a Boolean tag $b$, if $\tau_O(z_O)$ is blank, then one step of the constructed machine from its waiting-decision configuration halts and outputs the single bit answering the decoded selector from $oq$, $r$, and the symbols currently scanned by $c$.
hypotheses_covered: M is a finite-state Turing machine over Boolean symbols
x and y are Boolean words
bits is a Boolean selector encoding
P is a valid input-head position for y
